subject: Re: PineStreet — deployment path & dedicated sizing follow-up

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: PineStreet discovery — post-call recap + clarifying asks

Thanks again for the time today, Dana — really helpful conversation. Quick recap and a few clarifying items so we can size a dedicated pool that meets your performance and residency needs. Attaching the short PoC spec we mentioned (pinestreet_poc_spec.pdf).

Summary of what I captured from today
- Preferred deployment: leaning toward Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for low p99 latency and data residency; you flagged Private VPC as a requirement if procurement insists on customer-managed networking.
- Traffic profile (your stated targets): peak ~200 TPS at burst, sustained ~45-60 TPS; average request size ~350 tokens prompt + ~120 tokens generated = ~470 tokens total (you said some calls are longer for summarization flows).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + inbound audit requests; procurement wants network diagrams and KMS options.

Open clarifying asks (please confirm):
1) Is the 200 TPS a short burst (e.g., 30s-2m) or sustained for longer windows?
2) Token distribution: are ~25% of requests embeddings-only (short tokens), ~60% generation, ~15% rerank/qa? If you can share a small token_profile.csv, that would help.
3) Any hard latency SLO (p50/p90/p99) we should target? You mentioned p99 < 250ms as ideal for core search endpoints.

Initial sizing notes we plan to run after you confirm the token mix:
- GPU family options to evaluate: H100 (latency-optimized) vs A10G-like instances (cost-optimized for throughput). We’ll produce a headroom plan with both.
- Concurrency strategy: mix of model pinning (dedicated H100 for low-latency flows) + batchable A10s for cheaper background workloads.

Next steps
- Dana: please attach token_profile.csv and confirm whether 200 TPS is sustained or a short burst (reply here).
- We'll schedule a 45-min sizing workshop (karthik + ben + infra) after we get the token profile.
- If procurement wants vendor security docs, I’ll loop in our security contact next.

Thanks — I’ll hold a calendar slot tentatively for Tue morning next week for the sizing workshop but can shift based on your availability.

— Lauren Bishop

Thanks Lauren — that recap looks right. A few quick clarifications inline: 

- 200 TPS: that is a hard peak we expect during product launches; typical bursts are 2–5 minutes but could be repeated several times per hour. We also expect sustained traffic of ~50 TPS for business hours on weekdays.
- Token mix: I attached token profile export (pinestreet_token_profile.csv). Approximately~20% embeddings, ~65% generation (50% short replies ~200 tokens, 15% long generations 600+ tokens), 15% rerank/QA.
- Latency: our primary user-facing search experience needs p99 < 250ms; non-user-facing batch jobs can run up to 1s.

Procurement note: we prefer Dedicated for performance, but procurement will want a Private VPC deployment if we move to annual committed capacity. Will need KMS integration and IP allowlist. Timeline: negotiating budget this quarter — hope to finalize platform decision by end of April.

Happy to take a sizing workshop next week. Can you include an approximate cost band when you share initial numbers? Procurement will need order-of-magnitude cost to route internally.

— Dana

  Option A (latency-first): H100-heavy pool to hit p99 < 250ms at peak.

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>

Nice summary — I ran a quick pass against the token_profile.csv Dana sent and our profiling results for the Llama-3-70B quantized variant they mentioned on the call. High-level recommendation below (numbers are conservative with ~20% headroom for burstiness):

Assumptions from profile: median total tokens/request ~420, weighted average ~480 (because of long-gen tail).
Peak target: 200 TPS sustained for short bursts (2–5m). Sustained: 50 TPS. p99 target: <250ms for search endpoint traffic.

Perf estimates (per our profiler):
- H100 (latest NVLink H100 flavor): ~18–22 requests/sec per GPU at 480 tokens/request when tuned for latency (concurrency 6–8, low-latency kernels). p99 ~120–220ms depending on exact prompt structure.
- A10G-class: ~7–10 requests/sec per GPU at same token size when optimized for throughput (higher batching, concurrency 18–24). p99 is higher (400–800ms) unless we isolate short flows.

Sizing options (including ~20% headroom):
Option 1 — Latency-first (Dedicated H100 pool):
- Target: handle 200 TPS peak entirely on H100s for simplest operational profile and easiest p99 SLAs.
- Recommended: 11 H100 GPUs (200 / 18 ≈ 11.1 -> + headroom => 13, but we can start with 11 committed + 2 burst).
- Notes: higher monthly cost, simplest for p99 constraints and fewer routing rules.

Option 2 — Hybrid (latency-critical H100 + throughput A10s):
- Split: route user-facing search (estimated 60% of peak traffic during launches = 120 TPS) to H100 pool; route embeddings/batch/rerank to A10s.
- H100 count: 120 / 18 ≈ 7 -> recommend 8 H100 (including headroom).
- A10 count: remaining 80 TPS peak handled by A10s at ~9 TPS each -> 9 A10s (80/9 ≈ 9). Add 2 spare A10s for buffer => 11 A10s.
- Operational complexity: routing + autoscale policies, but much lower committed cost than all-H100 option.

Other notes and config knobs:
- Concurrency caps: set H100 concurrency to 6–8 for p99 targets; A10 concurrency 18–24 to maximize throughput.
- Batching/cache: for rerank and embeddings we can enable aggressive batching; for search we should favor low-latency kernels and KV cache pinning.
- Private VPC: we support Private control plane + KMS. Provisioning lead time for Private is ~4–6 weeks from PO (includes networking, firewall rules, KMS integration). Dedicated hosted (no VPC) is faster: ~2–3 weeks.
- Cost band (very rough): Option1 (all H100 committed pool) ~ $$$ (order magnitude: high); Option2 (hybrid) ~ 40–60% of Option1. I will prepare a tighter ballpark for procurement once we pick exact instance sizes and discount tier.

Next steps I propose:
1) Run a 45-min sizing workshop with PineStreet (include their infra/procurement) — we’ll fill the calc sheet and pick Option1 vs Option2.
2) After workshop, produce a 1-page committed-capacity proposal with costs and lead times and a short runbook for failover to hosted API in case of capacity events.

I can be on the sizing call Tue 10–11am or Wed 1–2pm PT — which works for PineStreet?
